content.text: {"relation":"MATCH","consensus_summary":"Across all four blind responses, the dominant reading is that a garment symbolizes a person's spiritual state and standing before God — above all righteousness/salvation. Clean or white garments represent righteousness (understood either as imputed righteousness from God/Christ or as the righteous deeds of the saints, a recognized intra-consensus debate), while filthy garments represent sin. Key texts include Isaiah 61:10, Zechariah 3:3-5, Matthew 22:11-14, Galatians 3:27, and Revelation 3:4-5, 7:13-14, and 19:8. Secondary contextual uses (status/office, old-new self, resurrection body, covering of shame) are acknowledged as distinct.","book_summary":"The book identifies the garment as 'Righteousness — the righteous acts of the saints,' citing Revelation 19:8 (ASV), which explicitly glosses the fine linen as the righteous acts/righteousness of the saints.","consensus_core_identification":"Garment = righteousness / the wearer's spiritual standing before God (whether imputed by God or expressed in the saints' righteous deeds).","book_core_identification":"Garment = righteousness, specified as the righteous acts of the saints (following Rev 19:8's own interpretive gloss).","core_relation":"EQUIVALENT","extension_relation":"SAME_CASES","boundary_disagreement":"The only potential boundary issue is that the book's gloss adopts the 'righteous deeds of the saints' side of the well-known imputed-righteousness vs. righteous-deeds debate, which could be read as excluding the imputed-righteousness construal (e.g., Isaiah 61:10, Zechariah 3). However, the consensus itself explicitly treats both construals as positions within the same broad symbolic field, so this is an intra-consensus wording choice rather than a material boundary change. The glossary entry also does not mention secondary uses (status/office, resurrection body, mourning), but as a primary-meaning gloss this omission does not create disagreement.","material_contradiction":"None. The book's identification sits squarely within the consensus's primary meaning and even quotes the consensus's own leading proof text's internal interpretation.","rationale":"All blind responses converge on garment = righteousness/spiritual standing before God, and every response cites Revelation 19:8 among the primary bases — the very verse the book prints, whose own text defines the fine linen as 'the righteousness [righteous acts] of the saints.' The book's core identification (righteousness) is equivalent to the consensus core. Its choice of the 'righteous acts of the saints' phrasing tracks one recognized side of an intra-consensus nuance that Response A explicitly says remains 'within the same broad symbolic field.' There is no replaced referent, no boundary redrawing of substance, and no contradiction; the differences are wording-level.","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"One could argue for REFINED on the grounds that 'the righteous acts of the saints' narrows righteousness to sanctified deeds and implicitly rejects the imputed-righteousness reading favored in much Protestant teaching (Isaiah 61:10, Zechariah 3:3-5), thereby excluding cases where the garment is a divine gift rather than the believer's works. But since the consensus explicitly houses both construals within its primary meaning, and the book's gloss is simply Rev 19:8's own wording, this objection does not establish a material boundary change.","confidence":"high"}
